text: 54-year-old male. The patient has been experiencing a gradual difficulty in walking over the past 3 months, requiring wheelchair assistance for the last month. speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS).

The clinical picture of progressive lower motor neuron weakness (gait difficulty requiring a wheelchair), upper motor neuron signs (speech slurring, urinary incontinence suggesting sphincter dysfunction), and a chronic, progressive course in a 54-year-old male is highly suggestive of ALS. Given the rapid progression over three months, I request immediate MRI of the brain and cervical spine to rule out compressive myelopathy, followed by EMG/NCS for definitive confirmation of upper and lower motor neuron involvement.
